plan.english: If a wolf devours a sheep and the shepherd does not guard it, let that shepherd pay the king ten piglets. And if he guards it, let him pay nothing. If an eagle seizes a piglet, let him pay nothing.

Whoever steals a stallion in the night, let that thief give seven sheep. And if he drives it away, let him lead a hundred cattle to the king. If the driver sees the thief at dawn, let him seize him and lead him to the king. If the thief flees, let no one kill him. Let the dog seek the track of the thief.

Whoever breaks the wall of the settlement, let that man build it again. But if the snow splits it, let no one pay. If a wild animal tears up the pen of a mistress, let her build it. The wall shall stand, and the free men shall guard it.
If a dog kills a piglet in the pen, let its mistress give a sheep to the son. If he kills a wolf, let her give nothing. If a dog eats a raw bird, let her cover it.
Let no one plough the field of his sister. If a man ploughs it, let her seize the two yokes of that man. If the cattle of that man enter the field and eat, let him give her wool.
Whoever burns the cow-stall of a free man, let him build it again and lead ten sheep. If the wind carries the fire to the stall, let him give nothing. Let the free man seek the thief with his dog.
Let no one kill a guest. Let him be dear to the gods. Let him sit, and let the mistress clothe him. Whoever kills him, let the king drive that man out.

Whoever breaks the oath, let his name vanish from the kin, and let no one give him fire and water. Whoever does not deceive and does not break the oath, let his name be famous. May the sky give him good fame.
If a man leads a sister to his home, let him give the bride price to her mother. Let her be free. If he does not give it, let the mother lead the sister back.

Whoever speaks a lie to the king, let the word of that man not be heard again, and let him go out of the settlement. Whoever hears a lie and tells it to the king, let him have a reward. The word of a free man is dear to the sky.
If a herd of cattle enters the field of a free man and eats, let the shepherd lead two sheep to him. If he drives the herd out of it at once, let him give nothing. Let the herd drink at the spring.

Let the mortal drink the water of the spring. Whoever urinates in the spring, let the men drive that man away from it. Whoever drives his own herd into the spring, let him lead a sheep to the kin. Let no one cover the spring.
If a man breaks the wheel of a driver, let him give the driver a yoke and a rope. If the wheel breaks, let the driver build it again, and let no one pay him.

Whoever snatches a bird from the net, that man is a thief. If he snatches an eagle, let him give the king a stallion. Whoever lets the bird away from the net, let him make a net. The eagle is dear to the sky.

Sun, who sees the mortals, you know my word. This is my oath: I did not steal the bird, and I did not seize the wool. If I deceive you, may fire burn me, and may the earth devour me. But if I do not deceive, may you give me good fame. Great is your eye, and shining is your name.

Father Sky, giver of good things, and Mother Earth, hear us! We two have made this oath. Whoever of us breaks it, may the wolves devour him. May the oath stand. And whoever does not deceive, may he live. May we two remember the oath. May the sun and the dawn see us two.
Immortal fire, look at me! I did not steal the stallion of my brother. I did not drive it out of the pen. If I stole it, may you burn me. My son knows my heart. You are swift and shining.

title: The shepherd's oath by the water

plan.english: Water, I the shepherd did not eat the piglets of the king. The wolf devoured them in the night. I caught sight of him. If I ate them, may I be thirsty. Do not come to me. May the wolf not come to my herd. May the wind carry the beast away from me.
Son, make this oath and speak: I did not drive the cattle of the settlement. Do not deceive the gods. If you lie, may the gods not hear you. Then my heart will rejoice. You are dear to me.
The two brothers made the oath. Together we shall drive the herd. If one flees, let that one seize him. May our mother see our fame. May our herd grow. May our name be great among the kin.

title: The hero's pledge to the king

plan.english: King, giver of good things, I shall follow you. I shall not flee. If I flee, may my name not be famous. If I die, may my fame be imperishable. I shall guard your name. Your fame is great.

The men of this settlement made an oath to the men of that settlement. We shall not drive away your cattle. May the gods hear our word. Whoever breaks this oath, may his herd vanish. May our sons live. Let those two be friendly. May the sky above hear it.
Husband, I guarded your wool. I did not give it to the guest. My heart is good. If I lie, may the earth swallow me. I am dear to you.
Guest, you are dear to me. I shall give you fire and water. I shall protect you in my home. I shall not drive you away. Do not drive me away. May the sky protect us. May you live.
I go into the water. Gods, you see my heart. My word is not a lie. If I deceive, may the snake devour me. If I do not deceive, may the water carry me out. I am not afraid.
We built this wall in the field. Whoever breaks it, may his own cattle flee. May the wall stand. May the sun see it. May no beast tear it down. May the wall be white and great.
King, I am not a thief. I did not seize the stallions. I was in the field. They vanished. My dog caught sight of the thief. If I deceive, may the wolf eat my heart.

The shepherd came to the king and said: "My piglets vanished in the night. My brother stole them." That one said: "I did not steal them. The wolf devoured them." The king said: "Who saw the wolf? No one saw him. Brother, pay him the wage."

Two sons came to their father. One said: "This field is mine." That one said: "His word is a lie. You gave it to me." The father said: "Who ploughed it?" The first said: "I ploughed it." The father said: "Let the field belong to the one who ploughed it." That one went away.

At dawn the driver seized the thief and led him to the hero. He said: "This one stole my net. I saw him in the night." The hero said to the thief: "Did you steal it?" The thief said: "I stole it." Then he said: "Give him a rope, and go out."

In the night a wild animal devoured three piglets. The shepherd came to the hero, and he was afraid. He said: "I guarded them with my dog. My dog saw it." The hero said: "The dog does not speak." This one said: "I am not a thief." Then he said: "You are not a thief. You did not guard them. Give the gods one stallion." Then he sat down.

A mortal made the oath before the king: "I did not seize the wool of my brother." The brother said: "You deceived. I saw you in the night. The wool is in your home." The mortal said: "The gods see my heart." The king said: "They see it. You deceived. Pay him the wage." Then he gave the wage, and his name was not famous.

The driver came to the father of the sister and said: "I gave the bride price. Give me your sister." The father said: "You gave me no bride price." The mother spoke: "I saw ten sheep in the pen." The father said: "They are a bride price. Lead her to your home." The heart of the mother was glad.

In the night the stall of the free man burned. He said to the driver: "Your fire burned my stall." The driver said: "I did not burn it. The wind carried it into the stall." The mistress said: "Let no one give anything. Let us build the stall again together." The driver and the free man built the stall again.

The man led the shepherd to the king and said: "He seized my wool and gave no wage." The shepherd said: "I paid the wage. My sister saw it. Sister, speak!" She spoke: "He gave him the wage there." The king said: "His word is a lie. Let him give him a stallion." Then the sister's name was famous.

title: The guest who was driven out

plan.english: A guest came in the night to the home of the mortal. The mortal drove him away. This one said to the king: "He gave me neither fire nor water. He drove me away." The mortal said: "I did not know him." The king said: "A guest is dear to the gods. Give him fire and water, and let him dwell in your home." The guest sat down, and the mistress clothed him.

The son followed the track of his cattle and arrived at the home of the hero. He saw the cattle in the pen. He came to the king and said: "My cattle are in his pen. The track goes to him." The king said to the hero: "How did they come into your pen?" The hero said: "I do not know." Then he said: "You are the thief. Lead them back to the son." The son drove the cattle out of the pen.

A guest died in the settlement. His brother came to the father and said: "The men of this settlement killed my brother." They said: "A wild animal ate him." Then he said: "Let them make the oath. Whoever does not make it, let them drive that man out." They made the oath. The sky sees the oath.

Two men came to the king. One said: "The stallion is mine." That one said: "He lies. The stallion is mine." The king said: "Stand in the field and cry out. I shall let it go." It went to that one. Then he said to him: "It is yours." The first man led the stallion away.

title: The wool of the shepherd's wife

plan.english: The guest said to the mother: "The wife of the shepherd stole my wool." The mother said: "Wife, what are you saying?" She said: "The wool is mine. My sheep gave it." Then she said: "I have heard the words of both. Guest, give her a piglet." Her heart was glad.
